payload.title: 8 Engagement Ring Cuts and the Hands They Flatter
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s, affluent, interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences beyond that, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: A well-travelled couple in their mid 30s, about to propose or newly engaged, who have narrowed things down to 'it should be a diamond' and now want to know which shape will actually look right on the wearer's hand every day, at the proposal and in close-up ceremony photos abroad, without wading through grading jargon or a jeweller's sales pitch.
payload.goal: Click through to the destinations hub to start picturing where the proposal or wedding could happen (Wedded Concierge at /wonderland-concierge as secondary CTA).
payload.angle: Most 'ring cuts for your hand' articles hand out confident rules (this shape for short fingers, that one for wide hands) with no source and a whiff of 'fixing' the wearer. This guide separates what each of the 8 shapes does visually on any hand (lengthens, widens, softens, sharpens) from what GIA actually says about flattering hands, states a 'flatters' line only where GIA or a jewellery-education source supports it, and otherwise says plainly 'try it on' with a three-step try-on routine (photo from above, photo at arm's length, a day of wear) the couple can do in any showroom, at home or abroad. It reads every shape for proportion and preference, never as a correction, and adds how each shape reads in sun-lit outdoor ceremony photos.
must_include: Short intro: shape versus cut in plain words (in everyday speech 'cut' usually means shape; cut grade is a different thing, link /style-advice/diamond-buying-guide for grading) and how to use the guide: visual effect, what the source says, try it on

Cut 1: Round brilliant. Visually: balanced, symmetrical, maximum sparkle, neither lengthens nor widens. Sourced flatters line: GIA says round brilliant flatters almost any finger length and shape (re-check fact in engagement-ring-styles source pack). Fallback: compare a round with an elongated shape side by side on the same hand

Cut 2: Oval. Visually: elongated north-south outline lengthens the look of the finger; softer than a marquise. Sourced flatters line: GIA says elongated shapes (oval named) have a north-south axis that can accentuate finger length when set traditionally. Fallback: try north-south and east-west orientation; mention bow-tie only as a 'look for it in person' check, not as a sourced fact unless 03 finds a source

Cut 3: Emerald. Visually: step-cut rectangle, long clean lines, 'hall of mirrors' flash rather than sparkle; lengthens when set north-south. Sourced flatters line: only the GIA 'rectangular' elongated-shape line applies; anything stronger is try it on. Fallback: try in strong daylight; link the diamond guide for why step cuts show clarity more (sourcing still open)

Cut 4: Cushion. Visually: square to slightly rectangular with rounded corners; softens and reads vintage and romantic; a square cushion neither lengthens nor widens much. Sourced flatters line: none found in sister packs, so no flatters claim. Fallback: try it on, compare square and elongated cushions

Cut 5: Princess. Visually: crisp square with pointed corners, modern and geometric, sits compact on the finger. Sourced flatters line: GIA says princess flatters almost any finger length and shape (re-check). Fallback: try it on beside a cushion to feel the difference between sharp and soft corners; note corners are often protected by the setting and link the settings post rather than explaining mechanics

Cut 6: Pear. Visually: teardrop, elongates the finger, part round and part marquise, direction of the point is a personal choice. Sourced flatters line: GIA names pear among elongated shapes that can lengthen the look of the finger. Fallback: try point towards the fingertip and towards the wrist

Cut 7: Marquise. Visually: long boat shape with two points; the most lengthening of the 8 and can look larger face-up for its weight (only if 03 sources it). Sourced flatters line: GIA names marquise among elongated shapes that can lengthen the finger. Fallback: try north-south and east-west; points are protected by the setting, link the settings post

Cut 8: Radiant. Visually: rectangle or square with trimmed corners, combines step-cut outline with brilliant sparkle; elongated radiants lengthen, square radiants sit compact. Sourced flatters line: GIA 'rectangular' elongated-shape line applies to elongated radiants only. Fallback: try both proportions
Asscher: one line acknowledging it as the square step-cut alternative to emerald and that it can swap in for any of the 8 if the SEO researcher finds stronger demand
A short 'what each shape does' quick-reference table (shape, visual effect, sourced flatters line or 'try it on', mood) with no prices and no grading detail

A neutral hand-and-finger section using GIA guidance rewritten without gendered language: simple designs for shorter fingers, wider bands for larger fingers if comfortable, long slender fingers carry the widest range, the wedding band alongside changes the look; framed as proportion and preference, never as fixing a flaw

A 'try it on' routine: photograph from above and at arm's length in daylight, wear for a day if a mock-up is offered, try with the intended wedding band, and check how it reads in sunlit outdoor ceremony light

Internal links (no repetition of their content): /style-advice/diamond-buying-guide (shape and grading), /style-advice/engagement-ring-styles (overall looks), /style-advice/engagement-ring-setting-for-active-lifestyle (how the stone is held), /style-advice/celebrity-engagement-rings (real examples by shape), /expert-advice/how-much-should-you-spend-on-an-engagement-ring, /proposal/how-to-propose-a-step-by-step-guide-to-the-perfect-moment
Soft bridge to /destinations (primary) and /wonderland-concierge (secondary), using only claims from brand-facts.md; UTM-tag every CTA

Reuse and re-check GIA facts from content/posts/diamond-buying-guide/03-source-pack.json and content/posts/engagement-ring-styles/03-source-pack.json (source: 4cs.gia.edu engagement-ring-styles-to-flatter-hands-fingers)
avoid: Any price figures, price ranges or 'shape X costs less per carat' claims
Naming or recommending jewellers or brands
Grading detail (cut grades, colour and clarity scales, carat, reports); link the diamond buying guide instead
Settings mechanics (prong types, bezel detail, head height); one line and a link to the settings post
Repeating ring styles (halo, three-stone, toi et moi) as sections; link the styles post
Celebrity ring examples beyond one passing link to the celebrity rings post
Unsourced 'flatters' claims or rules such as 'shape X for chubby or stubby fingers'; if GIA or a jewellery-education source does not support it, describe the visual effect and say try it on
Gendered or body-judging language ('her hand', 'slim down', 'hide', 'fix', 'chubby', 'stubby'); use 'the wearer', 'longer or shorter fingers', 'wider or narrower hands'
Invented popularity statistics or trend percentages for shapes unless sourced
Copying wording, structure or images from jewellers or competitors, including Easy Weddings
Business details not in brand-facts.md (fees, a named Advisor, Wedded Privileges specifics are deferred)
Em dashes and US spelling (use jewellery, colour, travelling, organise)
